headline.title: Supermarket chain swaps self-checkouts for staffed tills
headline.dek: After a six-month trial, Pantry & Co brings back cashiers in 120 of its 310 stores by March.

scenes.question: What's changing?
scenes.why: The news is a switch from one way of paying to another, which is exactly what this format shows.

scenes.question: Did the trial work?
scenes.why: Three trial results, each with a direction the article states.

numbers.label: Fall in losses from theft and scanning mistakes
Average wait to pay, down from 6

scenes.question: How big is the rollout?
scenes.why: The switch grows in three steps, from the trial to the full rollout.

levels.text: Six-month trial: staffed tills in 12 stores

scenes.question: Will other chains follow?
scenes.why: The analyst sets out the choice other chains face; the article gives both options.

data.right: Wait for a full year of results

scenes.question: Who's saying what?
scenes.why: The chief executive's reason and the analyst's doubt, side by side, so both sides are heard.

comments.speaker: Marta Lindqvist
comments.text: People told us they were tired of arguing with a machine about an unexpected item in the bagging area

comments.speaker: Priya Nair
comments.text: [Staffed tills] cost more every single hour, and the savings from lower theft may not last

bottom_line: Shoppers in 120 stores will mostly pay at a till again, but every store keeps at least two self-checkouts.
